task: Built and tested a vault file management system with S3/R2 storage, two-stage upload UX, per-file assignment menus, bulk selection, and file move/copy logic distinguishing user uploads from main-app files.
discussion_summary: The vault is a standalone owner page connected to Cloudflare R2, allowing users to upload files to an Inbox, then assign them to category buckets (experts, portfolio, pitched, resources) matching the QCI Club header menu. Files are organized by category and optional subfolders; Resources has 4 fixed tabs (Understand, De-Mystify, Analyze, Learn) mirroring the public Resources page. The backend uses FastAPI with asyncpg and boto3; the frontend is Next.js with React. Vault-managed files (inbox, vault, categories) are moved on assignment; main-app files (applications/, project IDs, canvas-policy/, test/) are copied to preserve originals. Published Resources files are marked and cannot be reassigned. The vault table now includes checkboxes for bulk selection, per-row assignment menus, and a bulk bar showing selected count with an Assign option. All workflows have been tested in Chrome with real R2 objects.

decisions.decision: Vault file uploads are categorized into four buckets (experts, portfolio, pitched, resources) matching QCI Club header menu structure
decisions.reason: Mirrors existing site navigation; allows content organization by type; enables category-specific access control and retrieval in future features

decisions.decision: Vault upload UX is two-stage: drop zone queues files as draggable chips; drag each chip onto a category tile to upload it
decisions.reason: Prevents accidental uploads to wrong category; gives user explicit control over destination; reduces cognitive load vs. single-step upload with category selector

decisions.decision: S3/R2 storage keys are prefixed with category name: {category}/{uuid}/{filename}
decisions.reason: Enables logical grouping of files by category in object storage; simplifies future queries and access policies; mirrors frontend category structure

decisions.decision: Vault-managed files (inbox, vault, categories) are moved on assignment; main-app files (applications/, project IDs, canvas-policy/, test/) are copied
decisions.reason: Preserves main-app file integrity and location tracking; allows vault to manage its own files without breaking investor app dependencies

decisions.decision: Resources has 4 fixed tabs (Understand, De-Mystify, Analyze, Learn) with per-tab validation rules (kind, category, published_on, platform) stored in resource_items table
decisions.reason: Mirrors public Resources page structure and filters; enables granular content curation; database row tracks metadata for API and frontend display

decisions.decision: Published Resources files show 'Published' tag in vault table and cannot be reassigned via normal assign workflow
decisions.reason: Prevents accidental modification of published content; makes publication status visually clear; enforces one-way publish semantics

decisions.decision: Vault file table includes checkbox column with select-all header, per-row 'Assign to…' menu, and bulk selection bar ('N selected · Assign to…')
decisions.reason: Allows users to assign multiple files at once; per-row menu enables single-file assignment; bulk bar is always rendered with visibility:hidden to prevent layout shift

decisions.decision: Backend uvicorn startup requires --env-file .env flag to load DATABASE_URL and other environment variables
decisions.reason: app.main.py does not call load_dotenv(); uvicorn must be explicitly told to load the .env file or environment variables will not be available at app startup
